members.name: create_prompt
members.doc:
Create a prompt.

Parameters
----------
context : Context | Sequence[Context]
    Context or list of contexts. Each context is a sequence of entries
    where each entry is a raw sequence (``bytes``/``str``, optionally with
    ``:`` chain breaks for multichain), [`Protein`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein), or
    [`Complex`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Complex). Only protein chains are accepted; passing a
    Complex with DNA, RNA, or Ligand chains raises
    [`InvalidParameterError`](/references/python-api/openprotein#openprotein.errors.InvalidParameterError).
name : str
    Name of the prompt.
description : Optional[str]
    Description of the prompt.

Returns
-------
Prompt
    The created prompt.

parsed.text: Create a prompt.

members.name: create_query
members.doc:
Create a query.

Parameters
----------
query : bytes or str or Protein or Complex
    A query protein or complex. Raw ``bytes``/``str`` inputs may include
    ``:`` chain breaks to denote a multichain protein. Only protein
    chains are accepted; passing a Complex with DNA, RNA, or Ligand
    chains raises [`InvalidParameterError`](/references/python-api/openprotein#openprotein.errors.InvalidParameterError).
force_structure : bool, optional
    Optionally force a query to be interpreted with a structure.
    Useful for creating structure prediction queries which can have
    no structure.

Returns
-------
Query
    The created query.

parsed.text: Create a query.

members.name: get_as_complexes
members.doc:
Retrieve the prompt context with every entry as a [`Complex`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Complex).

Single-chain entries are wrapped as ``Complex({"A": protein})`` so the
return type is uniform regardless of chain count.

members.name: get
members.doc:
Retrieve the prompt as context entries.

Single-chain entries collapse to [`Protein`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein);
multichain entries are returned as [`Complex`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Complex).
Use [`get_as_complexes`](/references/python-api/prompt#openprotein.prompt.Prompt.get_as_complexes) for a uniform ``Complex`` return, or
[`get_as_proteins`](/references/python-api/prompt#openprotein.prompt.Prompt.get_as_proteins) for a uniform ``Protein`` return (the latter
raises if any entry is multichain).

Returns:
    list of list of Protein or Complex representing the prompt context

members.name: wait
members.doc:
Wait for the job to complete, then fetch results.

Parameters
----------
interval : int, optional
    Time in seconds between polling. Defaults to `config.POLLING_INTERVAL`.
timeout : int | None, optional
    Maximum time in seconds to wait. Defaults to None. The timeout is
    checked between polls, and a stalled poll is retried before it
    fails, so the wait can run past it.
verbose : bool, optional
    Verbosity flag. Defaults to False.
**kwargs
    Keyword arguments passed to `get`.

Returns
-------
Any
    The results of the job.

Raises
------
TimeoutException
    If polling exceeds the timeout.
JobFailedException
    If the job was canceled and is a result future or stores outputs.
    A failed job raises on the read.

Notes
-----
A terminal status does not necessarily mean success. This method
updates the stored job and calls ``get``, whose errors depend on the
result reader.

members.name: wait_until_done
members.doc:
Wait for the job to complete.

Parameters
----------
interval : float, optional
    Time in seconds between polling. Defaults to `config.POLLING_INTERVAL`.
timeout : int, optional
    Maximum time in seconds to wait. Defaults to None. The timeout is
    checked between polls, and a stalled poll is retried before it
    fails, so the wait can run past it.
verbose : bool, optional
    Verbosity flag. Defaults to False.

Returns
-------
bool
    True if the job reached a terminal status (success, failure or cancellation).

Notes
-----
This method refreshes the stored job but does not fetch results, unlike
`wait()`. Check `status` for success or failure. A polling timeout raises
`TimeoutException`.

entries.name: Query
entries.doc:
Query containing a sequence/structure used to query the design models which opens up new workflows.

Create a query with a masked sequence using [`mask_sequence_at`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein.mask_sequence_at) for [`PoET2Model`](/references/python-api/embedding#openprotein.embeddings.PoET2Model) to run inverse folding.

Create a query with a masked structure using [`mask_structure_at`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein.mask_structure_at) for [`RFdiffusion`](/references/python-api/models#openprotein.models.RFdiffusion) to run inverse folding.

parsed.text:
Query containing a sequence/structure used to query the design models which opens up new workflows.

Create a query with a masked sequence using [`mask_sequence_at`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein.mask_sequence_at) for [`PoET2Model`](/references/python-api/embedding#openprotein.embeddings.PoET2Model) to run inverse folding.

Create a query with a masked structure using [`mask_structure_at`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein.mask_structure_at) for [`RFdiffusion`](/references/python-api/models#openprotein.models.RFdiffusion) to run inverse folding.

Retrieve the query as a [`Protein`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein) or  [`Complex`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Complex).

Single-chain queries collapse to [`Protein`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Protein); multichain queries are
returned as [`Complex`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Complex). For a uniform return type, see
[`get_as_complex`](/references/python-api/prompt#openprotein.prompt.Query.get_as_complex) or [`get_as_protein`](/references/python-api/prompt#openprotein.prompt.Query.get_as_protein).

Returns:
    Protein or Complex representing the query

members.name: get_as_complex
members.doc:
Retrieve the query as a [`Complex`](/references/python-api/molecules#openprotein.molecules.Complex).

An mmCIF or PDB query returns the parsed Complex with chain ids taken from the
file. A FASTA query has no chain id, so a single-chain result is
wrapped as ``Complex({"A": protein})``.
